standard.title: Develop production skills for meaning
standard.description: develop media production skills to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning through manipulation of media languages, including images, sounds, texts and/or interactive elements, and media technologies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can experiment with production techniques and evaluate how changes affect meaning. They can apply Foley sound, storyboarding and image review. They have not yet manipulated media languages across multiple forms to communicate perspectives — or applied genre conventions deliberately to create humour, mood or meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop media production skills to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning through manipulation of media languages and media technologies.

nodes.label: Manipulating media languages to change meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate at least two media language elements (sound, framing, editing, text, augmented environment) and explain how each manipulation changes the meaning or perspective communicated.
nodes.minimum_width: Manipulate one media language element (e.g. add or modify a soundtrack to an existing image sequence) and describe how the change affects the perspective or meaning communicated.
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate media languages across images, sounds and texts — framing to change status/power, sound and music to change mood, genre conventions applied to everyday events to create humour; use Viewpoints questions to evaluate the effect of each manipulation; experiment with augmented reality or chroma key to change environments.
wider: Trial applying the conventions of an established genre to an everyday event to create humour (e.g. a visit to the library as an action movie) — experimenting systematically with framing, music and sound effects, and evaluating how genre conventions create comic effect through audience expectation

Use augmented reality, virtual reality or chroma key to transport the same content into three different environments — comparing how the environment change creates different meaning and evaluating which is most effective for a specific audience
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot connect specific manipulation choices to their communicative effect, production decisions remain accidental — they cannot evaluate or refine their work against communicative intent.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions as an explicit evaluation frame: 'How can I change the meaning of a story by adding or modifying a soundtrack?' This builds the reasoning habit that distinguishes deliberate production from accidental production.

success_criteria: Student can manipulate at least two media language elements (sound, framing, editing, text)
Student can explain how each manipulation changes the meaning or perspective communicated

nodes.label: Production skills across forms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply production skills across multiple media forms — capturing, sequencing, scripting or documenting with deliberate communicative intent in at least two different task contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply production skills in two different media forms or task contexts (e.g. stop motion animation and radio script, or green screen film and podcast) — demonstrating deliberate manipulation of media languages in each.
nodes.typical_width: Develop production skills across a range of forms — comic book/animation/stop motion with green screen, genre conventions applied to everyday events, radio production script with permissions documentation, image-music meaning experiments; practise selecting the most effective approach from multiple options.
wider: Create a script for a radio production and document the permissions required for music and voice talent in a real-world community radio setting — practising the professional production workflow from scripting through to permissions documentation

Produce a stop motion animation or green screen work that retells a familiar story in a new environment — applying all stages of the production process and reflecting on how environment choice serves the communicative intent

response_modes.reason: Build students' production skill repertoire across multiple forms — animation, film, radio, print. The wider the repertoire, the more informed future production choices will be.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of production forms available at Y5-6 (stop motion, green screen, radio script, genre film, comic) is genuinely diverse — students who develop skills across multiple forms are much better positioned for the Y7-8 band's design-oriented production work.
success_criteria: Student applies production skills in at least two different media forms or task contexts
Student makes deliberate manipulation decisions in each and can explain the communicative intent behind those decisions
